transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what brought me in is... people keep saying I’m not listening to them. Mostly my wife, and my supervisor at the plant. 

I mean, it's probably not a huge deal, but they'll be talking straight to me, and... I don't know, a minute later I just realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to say it all again. I always feel awful about it because I really do respect them and I *am* trying to hear them, I just sort of... miss things sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Do you find it hard to stay focused or concentrate on things, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Um... no, I don't think so? I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself after what I just said about listening to my wife and my boss. But when I'm actually doing a task, like working my station on the line or fixing something up around the house, I can focus just fine. 

I actually really like keeping my hands busy, you know? I guess I just... I don't know, maybe I just have a lot of energy and get a little restless sometimes, so I'm always moving on to the next thing. But my concentration itself is usually okay, I think. I'm a really hard worker. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When people are talking to you, do you find yourself getting distracted easily or having trouble staying focused on what they're saying?

Um... no, I don't think I get distracted by other things. Like, I'm definitely not daydreaming or looking around the room when my wife or my boss is talking. 

I know I said earlier that I end up missing half of what they say, and I really do feel terrible about that... but it's not because my mind is wandering off to something else, if that makes sense? I'm really trying my hardest to lock in on them. I just... I don't know, maybe my brain is just moving too fast and I lose track of the words? But I'm definitely not just ignoring them or getting distracted by what's going on around us. I really do respect them and want to hear them. 

Is it alright that I don't have a better way to explain it? I'm trying to give you the best answer I can, I just don't want you to think I don't care about what people tell me.
Have you noticed any other changes in the way you think, like trouble remembering things, organizing your thoughts, or keeping track of what's happening around you?

Oh, no, I don't think so. My memory is actually really good, I promise. I never forget how to run the machines at the plant or the steps for a job, anything like that. 

And as far as keeping track of what's happening... I'm actually pretty good at that. If anything, I'm usually the one noticing everything going on on the floor because I'm always moving around and checking on things. But my thoughts definitely aren't disorganized or anything. I really try my best to stay on top of it all and do a good job. 

Is that... does that sound okay? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my edge or anything like that. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can with these questions, I just haven't really noticed any problems with my memory.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like you need to be moving or doing something, even in situations where you're expected to sit still?

Um... well, I guess I do move around a little bit, but I really hope it doesn't come across like I'm being disrespectful or anything. 

Like, if I’m sitting in one of our safety huddles at the plant, or even just at the dinner table at home... my leg is usually bouncing. Or my hands are busy messing with a pen or my keys, something like that. Sometimes the guys at work will tell me I’m shaking the whole bench we're sitting on. I always apologize right away when they point it out, because I really don't mean to bother anyone. 

I just... I'm so used to being on my feet and working hard, sitting perfectly still is just a little tricky sometimes. But I'm not trying to be disruptive, I promise. I just have a lot of energy to burn, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay answer, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need without sounding like a bad employee.
Do you ever find yourself acting quickly without thinking things through first, like interrupting others, making sudden decisions, or saying things before you mean to?

Um... well, I guess I do sometimes jump in a little early. But I really don't mean to be rude, I promise. 

Like, when we have our shift meetings and the supervisor is asking something, I... I kind of just blurt out the answer before he's even finished asking. And then I realize I'm already talking and I didn't even let him get to the most important part of what he was saying. I always feel awful when I do it, and I try to apologize right away. 

I just... I get so eager to help out and show that I know what's going on, you know? I think my brain just gets a little ahead of itself. But I really do respect my boss and I'm not trying to talk over him or anything like that. 

Is it okay that I do that sometimes? I mean, I know it's not great, but I really am trying to be a good team player. I just hope he doesn't think I'm being disrespectful.
